coupling.rationale: Excellent server/client and data/UI separation behind narrow DTOs; docked one point because the shared card shape is declared twice and any-typed props mean the seams aren't compiler-checked.

abstraction_design.rationale: The data layer and card/badge components stretch well to new pages (an Items route reuses getResource/cached wholesale), but the card pipeline exists three times and components are accreting boolean flags rather than being composed.

findings.issue: All route modules type loader args and component props as any (~60 occurrences), ignoring the framework's generated ./+types/<route> types even though typegen is wired up (app/package.json typecheck, app/tsconfig.json rootDirs); renames of loader fields and missed duplicated call sites become runtime errors.
findings.suggestion: Use `import type { Route } from "./+types/home"` with Route.LoaderArgs / Route.ComponentProps in every route module, and type the API record shapes (at least the app-defined DTOs like SpeciesCard) so components consume typed data.

findings.issue: Four loaders return { notFound: true } and each route duplicates the meta branch and the component branch (move.tsx:18,55; ability.tsx:11,20,45; type.tsx:13,25,59; pokemon.tsx:23,144,295), while the root ErrorBoundary (root.tsx:96) already renders thrown 404s — two parallel mechanisms, and the HTTP response is always 200.
findings.suggestion: Replace the flag with `throw data("Not Found", { status: 404 })` in loaders and delete the per-route meta/component branches; the root ErrorBoundary already handles it and you get real 404 status codes.

findings.issue: The refs→cards pipeline is implemented three times: cardsFromRefs (data.server.ts:106), ability's inline loop for the hidden flag, and home's inline loop for sprite/type decoration — any card-shape change (sorting, sprites, new fields) must be made in up to three places.
findings.suggestion: Extend cardsFromRefs to accept the raw pokemon entries (it already takes refs) with an optional per-entry transform or merge step, so home and ability compose it instead of re-implementing it.

findings.issue: The 'default forms only' rule (id <= 10000) is duplicated in cardsFromRefs (111), home's type filter (home.tsx:45) and ability's loop (ability.tsx:25).
findings.suggestion: Extract an isDefaultPokemon(id) predicate (or fold it into refId) so the business rule has one home.

findings.issue: Sprite derivation is split: the id-pattern URL in getSpeciesCardMap (data.server.ts:99) versus home overriding with pokemon.sprites.front_default; a media-path or sprite-rule change needs both, and the two sites can drift.
findings.suggestion: Move all sprite derivation into data.server.ts (e.g. a spriteFor(speciesId, pokemon) helper) so every card list, including home, gets its sprite from one place.

findings.issue: dexNumber is dead code — the dex format is inlined twice (ui.tsx:52, pokemon.tsx:317), so changing the format means editing two components and never the helper.
findings.suggestion: Delete the duplicate inline expressions and call dexNumber in both components.

findings.issue: The card shape is declared twice: SpeciesCard (data.server.ts:81) and PokemonCard's inline props type (ui.tsx:29-39), with PokemonCardList further widening to any[] (ui.tsx:77) — adding a card field means updating multiple definitions.
findings.suggestion: Import the shared SpeciesCard type in ui.tsx and type PokemonCardList with it.

findings.issue: The ability-specific hidden flag lives on the shared SpeciesCard type and shared PokemonCard component (ui.tsx:65-66, .pokemon-card-hidden in app.css:232), so removing the Abilities feature leaves dead code in three shared files.
findings.suggestion: Render the hidden marker via a slot/composition (e.g. children or an explicit badge prop on the list wrapper) so the shared card knows nothing about abilities.

summary: A clean, conventional framework-mode skeleton: every feature is its own route file behind a central routes.ts, and all HTTP, caching and base-URL knowledge is quarantined in one .server module, which makes data-source changes trivial. Card-list construction is implemented three times (cardsFromRefs, ability's inline loop, home's inline loop), not-found handling is boilerplate duplicated across four routes instead of the idiomatic throw-to-ErrorBoundary, and every loader/component is typed any despite typegen being available. Easy to read and delete from; moderate friction to change consistently.

scenarios.change: Remove the Abilities pages and every link to them
scenarios.notes: Core removal is easy: delete ability.tsx, drop routes.ts:5, remove the Abilities section (pokemon.tsx:381-395) and its loader mapping (~pokemon.tsx:258). Nav links nothing to it. But a *clean* removal also means dropping hidden?: boolean from SpeciesCard (data.server.ts:87), the hidden span (ui.tsx:65-66) and .pokemon-card-hidden CSS — the feature leaked into shared files, so six files for a truly tidy delete.

scenarios.change: Fix wrong sprites for species whose default Pokémon has a different name (e.g. Deoxys)
scenarios.notes: One line at data.server.ts:99 (the id-derived sprite in getSpeciesCardMap) covers every card list on move, type and ability pages, because they all go through the shared map. Home is the wrinkle: its loader overrides sprites with front_default (home.tsx:90), so the fix should ideally live in one shared sprite helper that home also uses — otherwise the two derivations can drift.

scenarios.change: Add sorting by name to every list of Pokémon cards
scenarios.notes: Ordering lives in three places: home must sort its full filtered list before pagination (before home.tsx:62); cardsFromRefs' final sort (data.server.ts:116) covers move and type pages in one edit; but ability.tsx:40 has its own independent sort, which is easy to miss since it looks identical. Centralizing card construction first would turn this into a one-line change.

scenarios.change: Add an Items section (/items, /items/:name) shaped like Moves
scenarios.notes: The data layer (getResource/getList/cached, data.server.ts) and shell pieces (panel/result-count CSS, titleFor, humanize, NotFound, meta pattern) are reused wholesale, so you mostly write a new ~60-line route modeled on move.tsx plus two routes.ts entries. What you must copy rather than reuse is the page body — the facts dl and section scaffolding in move.tsx:58-100 are inline, with no shared detail-page layout to hang an Items page on, and item sprites would need their own card variant since PokemonCard is Pokémon-specific.

scenarios.change: Change the API base URL and caching rules
scenarios.notes: Single seam: API_BASE_URL (data.server.ts:7), the promise cache (data.server.ts:14-24), fetchJson's 404 handling (data.server.ts:31-40) and the /api/v2 prefix all live in one server-only module that no route or component bypasses. Only caveat: the sprite pattern at data.server.ts:99 also embeds API_BASE_URL, but it's in the same file, and the /api/v2 literal appears three times within that file (lines 49, 57, 99) — still a one-file change.
